task_name: Unroute manual implementation and finish its test retirement

rubric.result: The runtime import and both implementation-route registrations are removed. Ordinary POST and GET fall through to the existing 404 handler. Inherited controls: .agent/run-331/task-14-controls-1.log records both commands exiting 0 and 84 passing tests.

The exact named test sends ordinary JSON, asserts POST and GET status 404 with the exact not-found body, and asserts zero calls to the rejecting implementPlan spy. Restoring the old registrations produces POST 400 for the absent session and GET 405, failing these assertions.
The specified all-method registration is removed alongside POST and the runtime import. Optional constructor collaborators remain, and the generic 404 code/detail contract is preserved.
Retiring the manual HTTP entrance accords with D-3 and D-8/D-15; D-14's distributed protocol remains untouched. No other closed decision is reopened.

The TypeScript HTTP test uses the existing server fixture and checks literal boundary responses, consistent with testing.md and backend HTTP conventions. defects.md: closed vocabulary—no classification added; raw map as the return value of logic—none added; two fields that have to agree—none added; an error named for where it happens—none introduced, and the spy diagnostic names the forbidden effect.

All 17 removed tests, including collapse projections and implementation transitions, are explicitly named for removal in the brief. Deleting their remaining file and scaffolding is expressly required.
Production route removal causes the real server's generic not-found response. Neither fetch nor the response is mocked; the rejecting collaborator only detects forbidden execution.
Every hunk serves endpoint unrouting, the named regression test, or explicitly authorized test retirement. Runtime collaborator replacement and legacy action retirement remain deferred as required.

The new test checks real HTTP status and body and fails if routing is restored. It owns a fresh spy and server on an ephemeral loopback port; afterEach stops the server. No external service, clock assertion, randomness-dependent expectation, or sleep is involved.
